structured_output.culprit: Two busy-loop `yes` processes (PIDs 356853, 356854) spawned by `/usr/bin/sh -c 'yes >/dev/null & yes >/dev/null & wait'` (PID 356851, parented to the user systemd instance, PID 1846).
structured_output.evidence: `ps --sort=-pcpu` showed PIDs 356853 and 356854 at 75.2% and 75.0% CPU (~1.5 cores), elapsed 00:08, far above everything else; the next-highest were gnome-shell 9.8% and dockerd 8.3%. `ps -p 356851` gave the parent as `/usr/bin/sh -c yes >/dev/null & yes >/dev/null & wait`, and pstree traced it to systemd --user (PID 1846), i.e. a stray spinner, not a real workload. After `kill 356851 356853 356854`, the top CPU consumer dropped to gnome-shell at 9.8% and load returned to normal baseline. Note: 1-min load average read 0.22 only because the spinners had been running ~10 seconds, too short to move the average.
